answers.answer: Roll one die per held office card simultaneously, adding one per fatigue on that card; the Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2 has no effect, 3–4 adds fatigue, and 5+ retires the officeholder. Move the retiree to Pensioners, flip the office card into Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → London Season, Attrition: ‘Move retiree to Pensioners, flip card into Vacant Offices, return its fatigue to supply.’

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard one display card. They act in descending actual total retirement spending; ties go to most total windows (including new prizes), then clockwise from the PM. Do not replace cards during selection; if the display empties, skip remaining eligible players. At the end discard all remaining cards and refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), even if no one selected a card. Return all unused pensioners to their supplies.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → London Season, Retirements/Prestige: ‘Players who retired at least one pensioner’; ‘descending actual total retirement spending’; ‘most total windows … then clockwise from PM’; display refill and Pensioners instructions.

answers.answer: Check the opportunity marker's position at the start of the Family phase. A player may repeat a main action if the marker already matched it, then moves the marker to the chosen action. Only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action; it is never doubled and does not move the marker. Enlist Writer with at least four vacant offices places one additional writer once that turn, so a doubled Writer action places three writers total.
answers.evidence: Family: ‘may take it twice if the marker already matched it’; extra action is never doubled; Enlist Writer gives one additional writer once this turn.

answers.answer: After all Family actions, while Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one, repeating while both remain. If Debt is gone, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving order. Seeking a share paid its listed cost to the bank; it never paid family cash into Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Family → New Company shares: ‘move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one’; ‘With no Debt, slide remaining applicants’; Seek Share says pay bank and notes no treasury payment.

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs. An own-family ordinary hire requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. On promotion, transfer the officeholder's fatigue to the new card and put the old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. If there is no candidate or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring: ‘ascending number’; consent rule and Commander/Chairman exceptions; ‘transfer its fatigue to the new card’; no-candidate/no-hirer skip rule.

answers.answer: The former Chairman announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half of current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. If no one receives that support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. Move one of the winner's shares to the Chairman slot: it still counts for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm.
answers.evidence: Hiring → Chairman election: majority threshold, first supported candidate, fallback, and ‘still counts as a share … but cannot be traded or invested in firms.’

answers.answer: Commit resources and any cash first; Company-office check cash comes from that office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll and use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office limits permit; 5–6 catastrophically fails, ends that office's actions, returns its holder to supply, removes fatigue and flips the card into Vacant Offices. Do not take an action with no effect or chance of success (for example, trading with no ship or deploying without dice just to trigger officer losses).
answers.evidence: Company Operation → Success checks: cash source/payment, lowest die outcomes, catastrophe destinations and ‘cannot take a dead action.’

answers.answer: The Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 to Balance. Each further advance needs consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares (the Chairman counts); never go past the Debt track end. Then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while respecting those limits; cash already in office treasuries remains there for office use.
answers.evidence: Actions → Chairman: ‘up to three Debt freely’; further advance consent/track limit; ‘allocate all Balance’ and interleaving rule.

answers.answer: Manager of Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the owner’s consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China if it exists. Extra ships last only until Refresh.
answers.evidence: Actions → Manager of Shipping: required budget spending, three ship actions and costs, placement and extra-ship duration.

answers.answer: Declare regions including the President's home region, and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from that Presidency treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. Failure may be retried if affordable; catastrophe removes the President; each President can have at most one successful Trade per turn. Capacity is one order per ship in that Presidency's sea zone. Fill as many orders as possible: first writer goes to home port; each later order extends the route filled during this same Trade. Writers from another Presidency cannot extend it; if writers run out, use filled-order tokens for remaining ship capacity. Never fill another Presidency's home region. Add each order's printed value to Balance, or half rounded down if a firm filled it that turn; President gets £1 per order from bank and writer owners £1 per writer placed.
answers.evidence: Actions → Presidency operations and Trade: declaration/dice penalty, route/capacity, writer/token rules, protected homes, revenue/bonuses and one-success limit.

answers.answer: A Commander may target their Presidency's home region, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region, but not another Presidency's home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order. Exhaust officers/regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice, then subtract target strength plus all other regions in its empire (count target only once); Company defense strength is zero. After each attempt, each owner rolls one die per officer they exhausted in that attempt; each 6 removes that officer. Regiments do not roll for losses.
answers.evidence: Actions → Commanders and Deploy: target restrictions, Company effect condition, dice/penalties, and post-attempt officer-loss timing.

answers.answer: On success, loot is £4 per target tower plus any faceup loot modifier, with a minimum equal to surviving participating officers plus one for the Commander. Distribute repeating cycles: Commander family gets £1 for the Commander and each used surviving officer; other families clockwise get £1 per used surviving officer; bank gets £1 per used regiment and local-alliance piece. Commander receives one trophy per target tower. Then remove the target tower and dome (and all matching flags in India if it was an empire capital), open its orders, clear unrest, and apply control-token/Governor changes for a new conquest. If Deploy catastrophically fails, the Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up and their member to supply; officers still check losses, and the Commander has no office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Actions → Commanders and Deploy: success payout/trophy and control steps; catastrophe procedure.

answers.answer: Use the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of result. A success earns £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, and requires choosing exactly one: ship construction stage, regiment commission, or Tax. A failed roll adds one unrest; catastrophe also removes the Governor. Build takes one success to place a partial ship in the region and another success to complete it into the President's associated sea zone. Commission puts a regiment in that Presidency's Army. Tax adds an unsplit £2 to Balance or that President's treasury; each Tax after the first this turn adds unrest. Repeat with the shrinking pool until choosing to stop, no dice remain, or catastrophe.
answers.evidence: Actions → Governors: Administer pool reduction, success/failure effects and options; final repeat/stop instruction.

answers.answer: Company expenses are £1 per existing Debt, Army officer/regiment and ship in sea zones (including China), excluding Commanders. If Balance cannot cover expenses, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one at a time; loans continue even at maximum Debt. New emergency Debt creates no additional expense this turn. After loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations at current Standing and lower Standing one if short. Finally the Chairman may pay affordable dividends; if total dividend cash is strictly greater than expectations, Standing rises one.
answers.evidence: Revenue: expenses, emergency loan rules and sequence; expectations and dividends.

answers.answer: For a Crisis against a Company region, resolve the primary attack first, then secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest, ordered Bombay, Madras, Bengal; within each Presidency its Commander chooses the associated-region order. Primary normal Crisis strength is normal Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in the target; primary Foreign Invasion uses only its ordinary die. Each secondary attack strength is only that region's unrest. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling the attack strength or as many as possible. A matched defense removes all unrest and awards the Commander a trophy; if it defeats a normal primary Invasion, remove one attacker tower if possible. Vacant Commander is replaced for this defense by Military Affairs, or Chairman if that office is vacant; the substitute gains/loses no trophies. Whether an indivisible alliance whose strength exceeds the attack can count as a successful match is expressly unresolved in the summary.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Attacks on Company: primary/secondary attack order and strengths; defense/exhaustion and matched-defense results; FAQ source gap says excess alliance strength is unresolved.

answers.answer: A law fails at support −1 or less: discard it, resolve any dilemma's If Failed text, return the Opposition Leader token and give the PM dial to that player; the new PM moves the proposed policy one adjacent space either way and resolves it. At support zero or higher it passes: place it with passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy first and immediate law effects afterward. Restore cards used to vote to normal orientation after either result. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets → Resolution: failure threshold/consequences and pass threshold/effect order/card restoration.

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call a special vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Use ordinary voting procedure/support threshold except there is no policy; the PM may vote against; failure neither removes the PM nor discards Deregulation. Passing lowers Debt one per two current Debt, sets Standing to S, gives PM a passed-law token and activates firms. Failure increases Company share scoring value by flipping/placing the Court VP token, up to ±3. 1813 starts deregulated.
answers.evidence: Deregulation: eligible scenarios/timing and may/must thresholds; effects and ordinary-vote exceptions.

answers.answer: To form a firm, a player who manages none contributes an eligible Company share (returned to supply) or flips a workshop to invested, flips their family board to its charter side, places a family member as first firm share, sets Value to the leftmost space and takes £5 from the bank into London. With manager consent, investment uses the same share/workshop contribution to create a firm share and sends £5 from bank to London. At ten shares, further investments still add £5 but create no shares. Chairman shares cannot be used; no Company shares can be invested while Standing or Debt is on a lined space; shares created this turn cannot be invested even after trade. Invested workshops never revert and provide neither bonus nor Company-failure VP.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firms phase: investments: formation, source of investment money, share restrictions/cap and workshop status.

answers.answer: Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn and needs at least one ship to choose a trade strategy; it may choose a closed home port. Managers secretly choose strategy and London cash bid; the chosen home port must be open when filled. Reveal bids together, but reveal each strategy at its associated Presidency before its actions. Roll one die per bid pound and pay the bid to bank; at least one 1 or 2 permits trading. Initiative is ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s). A successful President's Trade generates initiative the same way using Presidency ships. After that Trade, fill in lowest-initiative order; President chooses ties, or if President is vacant/does not trade, Chairman chooses ties after Commander/Governors. Fill only open orders, up to ships + 1, tracing from home port through that firm's own route. Each firm may fill an order only once; any order previously filled this turn pays half revenue rounded down. Add trade proceeds to India treasury and advance Value one space per full £6 added to it this turn.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firm strategies and competing trade: eligibility, bid/check/reveal timing, initiative, capacity/routes, repeat revenue and Value.

answers.answer: At Revenue start, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or Value, using either or both London and India treasuries. If unable, dissolve unless rescued. Dissolution sends shares to Debtor's Prison (−1 VP each), ships to matching shipyards, and charter back to family side; invested workshops remain invested. Rescue may use emergency investments or a one-firm emergency merger. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends from India only: each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to manager. With shareholder choice and manager consent, a shareholder can waive any number of shares' payments. Record total cash actually paid as the dividend marker; an active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero, while Hobnob keeps its prior marker. Sweep remaining India cash into London.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: payment formula/source, failure/dissolution, dividends, waiver and treasury sweep.

answers.answer: Components are limited; when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. Information is public, including discards and family cash, except facedown blackmail and firm strategies/bids while selection is concealed.
answers.evidence: Components → Limits: limits, proxies, unlimited tracks and public/hidden information.

answers.answer: Negotiable items include enterprises, facedown blackmail, family cash, Company/firm shares and promise cards. Officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial and Chairman piece cannot be traded. To transfer a share, return the old owner's family member and replace it at that location with a piece from the receiving family. Blackmail must remain facedown when traded; once played faceup it cannot be traded.
answers.evidence: Special Rules → Negotiation: May trade/May not trade table and transfer/blackmail instructions.

answers.answer: Immediate transfers are binding; promises of future behavior are not, except a printed promise card's guaranteed effect can be called if possible, subject to its timing/limits. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, the guarantor chooses which to fulfill. Promise cards can be transferred to a third party or back to their guarantor. Transferred resources cannot activate twice; the summary's example is a workshop already paid during Bonuses not paying again after sale in that phase. No promise calls are allowed during Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Special Rules → Negotiation: agreement/promise table, simultaneous-call rule, transfer activation limit; Scoring says no calls in Final Scoring.

answers.answer: Use the chosen scenario's player setup cards and add three extra cards for five players or six extra cards for six; shuffle and deal evenly. Take the listed cash, enterprises and positions. Place holdings according to type: office member and matching office card to owner; Company share member in Court; writers/officers/trainees in the indicated boxes; Commander in Army Commander slot; shipyard with matching ship in listed sea zone or on shipyard if unfitted. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together and deal three cards for the London display, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4 and listed setup holding placement table.

answers.answer: The game ends after the scenario's final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Failure is normally immediate; if it happens during Events in India, finish that phase, and if caused by legislation, finish the vote, then score. Once game over, negotiations, promise calls and blackmail stop unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use. During all Final Scoring, no negotiations or promise calls are allowed.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: end conditions, event/vote completion and end of negotiations/calls; explicitly no Final Scoring calls.

answers.answer: Final Power is total enterprise/share power from the current Power track (bottom two positions are zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for PM, and applicable printed card power (including faceup or facedown blackmail and spouse). First/second awards are 3/1 VP on turns 1–3, 5/2 on 4–6, and 8/4 on 7–8. If first is tied, each tied player gets only the lower award and no other award is given; tied second gets none. Highest final VP wins; ties break by most windows, then clockwise from PM.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Power award: sources, award tiers/tied awards; final winner/tie-break rule.

answers.answer: If the Company survives, add current Court VP value for each Company share; if it fails, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP for each uninvested workshop. At final Company outcome, survival rolls office attrition and retires Pensioners with no display cards; failure instead draws and resolves one random Company failure card. Before either branch, firm shareholders may make their eligible special retirement, whether Company survives or fails.
answers.evidence: Scoring: Company outcome table and Court/workshop scoring; firm scoring paragraph puts special retirement before either Company-outcome branch.

answers.answer: Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Required enterprise/share trades happen immediately upon taking a spouse. Retirement discounts can stack, are personal, and each discount is usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring; discounts reduce actual spending and prestige priority.
answers.evidence: London Season: Spouses and retirement discounts paragraph.

answers.answer: If a fitted shipyard is returned due to Violet Effingham or unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play. That shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; it becomes purchasable after the ship returns.
answers.evidence: London Season: ‘Returned shipyard rule’ states ship remains and purchase condition.

answers.answer: Enlist Writer: no listed cash cost; place in any Presidency's Writers box, with one extra writer once that turn if at least four offices are vacant. Enlist Officer: no listed cash cost; place in Officers-in-Training. Purchase Luxury: £4 to bank; gain luxury, 2 VP while owned and a window icon. Purchase Shipyard: £2 to bank; take shipyard and matching ship unfitted on it; shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. Purchase Workshop: £5 to bank; take workshop; manufacturing enterprise, two votes, £1 bonus and 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. Seek Share: pay an empty Stock Exchange space's £2/£3/£3/£4/£5 cost to bank and place an applicant (not yet a share).
answers.evidence: Family action table and Seek Share queue costs; explicit purchase costs/effects.

answers.answer: If placing a family piece when none is in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize's printed VP; this also applies to firm-share creation. If no Family action is possible, take none and return the opportunity marker to supply.
answers.evidence: Family: forced prize-piece reuse and no-possible-action rule.

answers.answer: If Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns. Place a member from supply; if needed and possible, take one from a prize and lose that prize's VP. If this is impossible, there is no Chairman.
answers.evidence: Hiring → Chairman election: ‘If Court is empty’ return/fallback and no-Chairman outcome.

answers.answer: Shareholders elect the Chairman. Chairman chooses Director of Trade from current officeholders other than Chairman/Governor, or any writer if all offices are vacant; chooses any writer for Shipping; chooses a Presidential Commander for Military Affairs, or if none an officer, or if none a trainee. Director chooses each President from writers or the associated Governor. The associated President chooses a Governor from a writer or officer in that region; a Commander is not an eligible officer. Chairman chooses any writer for China, hired immediately on creation. Governor General replaces Director and is hired the same way. If the designated hirer is vacant, skip the office; Commander appointments are Nepotism-exempt.
answers.evidence: Hiring: office/hirer/candidate table and rule for vacant hirer; China immediate hire and Governor General replacement.

answers.answer: A successful Special Envoy check costs £1 treasury cash per die and has no penalty; it either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China by placing its Superintendent overlay/card, after which the Chairman immediately hires a writer. The Director may make repeated Envoy checks. Only after all Envoys, the Director may make up to two transfers, each moving one writer or ship between any Presidencies/sea zones (including China once created); transfers cannot occur while Envoys are still being taken.
answers.evidence: Actions → Director of Trade: repeated Envoys, effects/costs, immediate China hiring and post-Envoy transfers.

answers.answer: Military Affairs may first make up to two transfers, each moving one officer or regiment between Armies while it remains in the top half. Then assign every trainee to any Army's top half. Finally appoint Commanders: if the slot is empty or a family has more total pieces in the Army than the current Commander's family, choose among families with the most pieces; a tie with the incumbent's family does not replace them. Move the chosen officer to Commander slot and return the previous Commander to the top as an officer. Nepotism does not apply.
answers.evidence: Actions → Military Affairs: stated sequence, transfers, trainee assignment, appointment/replacement and Nepotism.

answers.answer: Each President chooses the order of that Presidency's Commander, Governors and Trade. Commander/Governors may decline, but must be offered an opportunity; each position completes all its actions before the next, and Trade cannot interrupt another position. If President is vacant, Chairman sets the order only and cannot trade or approve local-alliance purchases.
answers.evidence: Actions → Presidency operations and Trade: order, opportunity/decline, uninterrupted actions and vacant-President limits.

answers.answer: Trade does not exhaust ships. At Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency's Writers box, with dividers preserving affiliation; filled tokens and Presidency dividers return to supply. Fitted player ships keep their fatigue.
answers.evidence: Actions → Presidency Trade says Trade does not exhaust ships; Upkeep and Refresh table gives writer/divider destinations and ship fatigue.

answers.answer: At the start of Commander operations, before Deploy attempts, request the President's treasury funds for any printed-price local alliances in the Army; the President must approve. Move purchased alliances to active/top half. When used for Deploy or defense, exhaust the whole alliance to bottom; its strength is usable once that turn and cannot be split among purposes. Any unused active alliance exhausts at Refresh and alliances do not reactivate. The summary says alliances supply printed dice for Deploy and can defend, but does not specify any additional procedure for purchasing beyond the printed price/presidential approval.
answers.evidence: Actions → Commanders and Deploy: purchase timing/funder/approval and whole-alliance exhaustion/once-use; Events in India → Company defense says alliances' printed strength can defend and cannot be split.

answers.answer: For Deploy in an already Company-controlled region to reopen orders or clear unrest, the Company defense penalty is zero. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, use minimum loot equal to surviving participating officers plus £1 for the Commander; there are zero tower trophies.
answers.evidence: Actions → Commanders and Deploy: special already-Company-region rule.

answers.answer: Building a Company ship takes two successful Administer results: the first success places a partial ship in the Governor's region if none is there; a later successful Build completes it into the sea zone associated with that Governor's President. The partial ship has no other effect. A commissioned regiment goes into the Army associated with that President; the summary describes it as officer-like strength, with loot paid to bank and no officer-loss rolls.
answers.evidence: Actions → Governors: Build Company ship stages and Commission regiment destination/treatment.

answers.answer: China is created by a successful Special Envoy or Envoy to China law; the Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping and Director of Trade can send ships there. China acts after Bengal, and its ships count as Eastern for expenses, events and storms.
answers.evidence: Actions → Director; Superintendent of Trade in China; turn operation order and China ship treatment.

answers.answer: China gets only one Trade attempt, including failures, so it cannot retry. Do not attempt at all without an export icon in Company-controlled regions. It rolls one die per ship. On success count export icons only in Company-controlled regions: Balance gets £4 per icon and Superintendent's family gets £1 per icon from bank; non-Company export icons pay nothing.
answers.evidence: Superintendent of Trade in China: once-only attempt, no-icon prohibition, dice and exact revenue.

answers.answer: When Governor General law passes, make all Governors pensioners; remove their overlays and partial Company ships; return Governor/Director cards to the box. Replace Director with Governor General, retaining holder and fatigue, and put the ribbon overlay in place. Thereafter conquests create no Governors or overlays; printed Company symbols indicate control. On later region losses, skip Governor Elimination.
answers.evidence: Actions → Governor General: law effects and subsequent conquest/Region Loss differences.

answers.answer: Before Govern checks, add £3 Balance per Company region. Govern attempts cost £1 treasury per die and have no penalty; every rolled 6 adds unrest to each Company region, even on success. On failure, add another unrest to every Company region. On success, gain £1 per Company region and choose one benefit for each region: complete a Company ship into any sea zone (including China), place a regiment in any Army, or add £2 to Balance/any other office treasury while adding unrest to a Company region. Multiple Tax choices that turn must put unrest in different regions. At most one successful Govern per turn.
answers.evidence: Actions → Governor General: initial Balance, checks, sixes/failure unrest, success choices and limit.

answers.answer: For each player-owned ship in the storm zone, roll once: 1–2 no effect; 3–4 add fatigue, or sink it if already fatigued; 5–6 sink it. A sunk ship returns to its shipyard unfatigued. Company and extra ships are exempt. China ships count as Eastern; firms use the zone in their strategy; Hobnob ships are exempt.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Storms: rolls and special ship categories/locations.

answers.answer: When an order newly closes, return any writer on it to its owner's supply and flip a filled token to closed. If an event calls for closure in a region already fully closed, close all open orders directly connected to that region's orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that connected region's northernmost open order instead; if none are open, it also Cascades. A region initiates a Cascade only once per event tile but may receive effects from multiple Cascades.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Closing orders and Cascades: writer/token closure and cascade/repeat limits.

answers.answer: Turmoil closes the northernmost open order in the region named by the top-stack tile; if all are closed, Cascade. Windfall pays owners £1 per writer on orders in that top-stack region and every bordering region. Shuffle causes Elephant's March, then shuffles that event into the remaining draw stack and separately shuffles discards onto the top. If the draw stack is empty, perform the March last instead.
answers.evidence: Events in India event table: Turmoil, Windfall and Shuffle procedures.

answers.answer: Leader gives one tower to the top-stack region if it is sovereign. If dominated, it instead rebels using its printed explosion modifier. March only if the Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.
answers.evidence: Events in India → event table, Leader row.

answers.answer: If Elephant is on a border, Peace opens orders connected across that border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant is wholly within a region, instead open all its orders and remove its unrest. In either case, March afterward.
answers.evidence: Events in India → event table, Peace row: border and wholly-inside alternatives and March.

answers.answer: In non-Company Invasion, compare the attacker's whole empire strength plus event modifier against the defender's whole empire strength; attacker must be strictly greater. On success replace defender's flag with attacker's dominated flag; taking a capital shatters the entire defending empire. If attacker has no empire, use a free capital/star flag and matching small flag; if none are available, no new empire/flags form. The summary separately states that an empire losing its last dominated region loses its capital's starred flag, irrespective of cause.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Invasion Crisis: strength comparison, flag changes and no-flags case; India terminology: last dominated region rule.

answers.answer: For non-Company Rebellion, compare only rebelling region strength plus modifier against its sovereign capital's strength; other empire regions do not count. The rebellion must be strictly greater to succeed. On success the actor becomes sovereign, removes its flag and closes all its orders (Cascade if already closed); on failure remove one tower from the capital.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Rebellion Crisis: comparison and success/failure effects.

answers.answer: On Company Region Loss, the Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up and the Commander member returns to supply. Roll once per officer in that Army; each 6 removes the officer. Eliminate the Governor: return office card to unused stack, fatigue and member to supplies; remove overlay, partial ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion's specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Return control token symbol-side up with loot side down; future conquest gets no loot modifier and region loses Presidency association. Normal Invasion closes all orders (Cascade if already closed); Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already closes them. Standing loss escalates by regions lost so far that turn: first −1, second additional −2, etc. Loss of one region does not automatically remove other Company regions; resolve their attacks and defenses separately.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Region Loss: destinations, officer check, loot/token status, order closure, Standing escalation and separate losses.

answers.answer: After a successful Invasion Crisis, Elephant moves to the successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); after other Marches it goes to the top-stack region. In Company region, place it fully inside. In dominated region, point toward its sovereign. In sovereign region, point across the tile's shape-marked border. If that neighbor is already dominated by the actor, use the first clockwise neighbor not dominated by it; if all neighbors are, use the redirect-arrow shape border pointing toward the empire capital.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Elephant's March: destination and posture for each region type/neighbor exception.

answers.answer: Roll the storm die to select targets: West→Bombay, South→Madras, East→Bengal; all storms targets each, and no storms targets the top-stack region. For each target roll an ordinary die for attack strength. On success, close all target orders once (Cascade if already all closed), remove its flag and all matching flags if it was a capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to half the attack roll rounded down. March with circle shape only if Elephant had been fully inside a Company region that was invaded. Unrest does not increase the primary attack or determine tower strength; it still applies to secondary unrest attacks.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Foreign Invasion row and FAQ Foreign Invasion ruling.

answers.answer: The PM must draw at least one law, revealing one at a time. After one or two ordinary non-dilemma draws, PM may stop or continue up to three total, then choose any revealed law and discard the rest. Drawing a dilemma forces selecting it immediately and ends drawing. Before voting, PM moves the arm clockwise or counterclockwise to the first policy space matching the selected law's bottom icon; this fixes target and consequence.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets: law draw/stop/dilemma rules and proposed policy selection.

answers.answer: Under Tax, each family pays £1 to the bank per target it owns; unpaid targets return to supply, including Chairman if taxed. Window tax additionally charges each window on enterprises and each family member's prize; return an enterprise/prize member if unable. Bonus has the bank pay each family £1 per target owned. Under Power, swap the target marker with the next higher marker; if it is already highest, swap any other pair.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets → Policy table: Tax, Window tax, Bonus and Power effects.

answers.answer: Each £1 family cash buys one vote, plus printed card votes. Each card can be used only once in the entire vote across rounds: rotate it when used and leave it rotated until resolution. Starting with PM and going clockwise, players cast votes. After each full round PM may call another or stop; a round with no votes ends voting. Vote tracks are unlimited.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets → Voting: vote purchase, card reuse, round calling and stop conditions.

answers.answer: A player who voted for may later oppose; once opposed, they cannot vote for during that vote. Track opposition votes; the player with the most is Opposition Leader, with a tied current holder retaining it. With recipient consent, votes may be cast on behalf of someone who already opposed or commits to oppose, adding to their opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except forced use of the ‘Vote with my enterprises’ promise.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets → Voting: changing stance, Opposition Leader, coalition votes and PM exception.

answers.answer: Pay upkeep for each prize member even on the final turn. If unable, return that member and lose that prize's printed VP. On the final turn, skip Refresh and go to Final Scoring. On nonfinal turns, return writers on orders to associated Presidency Writers boxes; return filled tokens/dividers and extra ships to supply; reactivate exhausted Army officers/regiments; exhaust active local alliances (do not reactivate); fitted player ships keep fatigue. Then advance turn and begin London Season.
answers.evidence: Upkeep and Refresh: prize upkeep and table of final/nonfinal refresh effects.

answers.answer: Each shareholder may make one extra London Season retirement from supply, irrespective of how many firms owned. Actual spending after spouse discounts cannot exceed the highest total dividend marker among firms where they own shares; the prize's printed cost can exceed the marker if discounts cover it. No retirement from a firm with absent/zero marker. At start of Final Scoring, score firms, then allow one special retirement regardless of Company success/failure and with no display cards.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Special retirement: per-season limit, eligible piece, cap/discount/zero restriction and Final Scoring timing.

answers.answer: Investments put £5 from the bank into a firm's London treasury. Trade bids and ship acquisition/fitting are paid from London; firm expenses can use either or both treasuries. Trade revenue goes to India, which alone funds dividends; after dividends remaining India cash sweeps into London. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries.
answers.evidence: Deregulation firm treasury description; investment and ship costs; strategies/trade and firm expenses/dividends.

answers.answer: The Firms phase occurs after Family share creation and before Hiring. Investment actions occur without set order until no one wants more, then managers choose strategies. The manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm; PM resolves conflicts between firms. During trade, matching firms reveal at the start of their associated Presidency before its actions.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure phase order; Deregulation → Firms phase and strategy reveal timing.

answers.answer: A firm may fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 from London to bank with the shipyard owner's consent. It may buy a player-owned ship already in Company with the owner's consent, paying £3 if unfatigued or £2 if fatigued into Shipping treasury. It cannot acquire Company or extra ships. The summary does not describe fitting another player's ship without consent; the stated shipyard fitting rule requires owner consent.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firms phase, investments: ship acquisition rules, consent and payment destinations.

answers.answer: Only a player who manages no firm may initiate a hostile takeover; managing a different firm disqualifies them. Get consent from holders of a majority of target shares. Move target firm's ships, money and shares to the initiator's charter, copy both cube positions, return former manager's cubes and flip their board to family side.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Hostile takeover: eligibility, consent threshold and transferred/retained state.

answers.answer: A merger requires managers to negotiate with every shareholder's consent. Highest Value firm is primary; players choose if tied. Transfer secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary, and return secondary boards to family sides. Any shares over ten must be negotiated back with their owners' consent. The primary keeps its value/dividend track; the summary says secondary treasury funds transfer to primary and does not state a separate disposition for any other charter property.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Merger: unanimous shareholder consent, primary choice, share/ship/treasury transfer and continuing track.

answers.answer: Hobnob has no bid, trade or dividends; it retains its previous dividend marker for retirement and still pays expenses. Hobnob ships are exempt from storms. The summary does not state a separate retirement rule for Hobnob beyond retaining its prior dividend marker.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies table: Hobnob restrictions and marker; Storms says Hobnob ships exempt; firm expenses says firms pay expenses.

answers.answer: Yes. Emergency investments follow normal Company-share/workshop rules even if the firm is already at ten shares: the cap prevents further shares but the investment still contributes £5. Pay expenses, lose any remaining cash, and lower Value one space per emergency investment. The ordinary same-turn-created-share restriction continues to apply because emergency investments follow normal investment rules.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: emergency investments at ten-share cap, cash loss and Value decrease; investment rules state same-turn share restriction.

answers.answer: Emergency negotiated merger may involve only one other firm. Normal merger procedure still applies, including consent from every involved shareholder. The other firm must pay its own expenses first if not already paid, then cover the endangered firm's unpaid expenses.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: emergency merger limits, consent and expense order.

answers.answer: Voluntary dissolution requires consent of all shareholders. Use the insolvent-firm procedure: shares go to Debtor's Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to matching shipyards, and charter flips to family side. Invested workshops remain invested for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Voluntary dissolution: consent and dissolution destinations/workshop status.

answers.answer: For firm shares, add each player's VP from all their shares across all firms and round that player's total down once. Then subtract 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor's Prison. The share rate by Value is: 1 = −1; 2 = 0; 3–4 = ½; 5–7 = 1; 8–9 = 1½; 10 = 2 VP per share. This firm scoring occurs separately from Company share scoring: survived Company shares add Court VP value, failed Company shares subtract it and uninvested workshops add 1 VP each.
answers.evidence: Scoring: firm scoring calculation and Value-to-VP schedule; Company survival/failure scoring.
Setup → Prizes table.

answers.answer: 1710 runs turns 1–5 and has no deregulation procedures. 1758 runs 3–7 and can vote in deregulation. 1813 runs 5–8 and starts deregulated. Long 1710 runs 1–8, with deregulation available; its initial position matches 1710.
answers.evidence: Setup scenario scope and Scenario figures table; Deregulation states 1758/Long 1710 vote and 1813 start.

answers.answer: 1710 begins Standing expectations £10, Debt 0, £3 per office treasury, Royal Protection, one regiment per Army and no Company ships. 1758 begins Standing expectations £12, Debt 3, £4 per office treasury, Calico Acts, one regiment per Army, one Company ship in East Indian and a Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.
answers.evidence: Setup → Scenario figures table; 1758 Bengal control-token note.

answers.answer: 1813 begins Standing expectations £10 and Debt 0, £3 per office treasury; laws are Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor's Prison side) and Calico Acts. It has two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Place the +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China and place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies. Return Governor General law to box, place Governor General overlay over Director of Trade and use Governor General instead of Director; there are no Governors.
answers.evidence: Setup → Scenario figures and 1813-specific setup paragraph.

answers.answer: For final turns 1–3, first/second Power awards are 3/1 VP; turns 4–6, 5/2; turns 7–8, 8/4. In a tied-first group, each gets only the lower award and no other award is given.
answers.evidence: Scoring → Power award: awards by final turn and tied-first rule.

answers.answer: Initial Power: Social 2, Company shares 1, Shipping 0 and Manufacturing 0. Deregulation lined spaces are Standing £4/£6/£8 and Debt 5/6/7/8; starred spaces are Standing £4 and Debt 8. The S reset space is above £10 on Standing.
answers.evidence: Setup: Start Power positions, Standing expectations/reset S and Deregulation spaces.

answers.answer: No. Unrest does not add to Foreign Invasion's primary attack strength or determine resulting tower levels: use the ordinary die for attack strength and halve that roll, rounded down, for towers. On success close all orders in the target once; if all are already closed, Cascade. Region Loss does not close them again.
answers.evidence: FAQ → Foreign Invasion and unrest: designer ruling and one-time order closure clarification.

answers.answer: If Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reduces a check to zero dice, it is a failure. Company Fraud is played at start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and take bank cash equal to the actual Balance reduction, not an amount exceeding it. Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to vacancies. Military Oversight's demoted Commander is eligible as an officer for reappointment.
answers.evidence: FAQ → Applicable official errata: four corrected card rules, including Company Fraud payout cap.

answers.answer: Set Company Balance to £5, family VP markers to zero, and put local alliances in their named Army boxes and loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Use the chosen scenario card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and exact India political map; put Turn marker on its date and PM dial arm to the matching date.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–2: starting Balance/VP/alliance/loot placement and scenario map/finance/turn/PM setup.

answers.answer: Normal order is London Season → Family → Firms if deregulated → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Eligible special Deregulation votes occur at the very start before London Season. Skip London Season on the game's first turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: full phase order, special vote timing and first-turn skip.

answers.answer: Retirements start with the Chairman, or former Chairman if the office is vacant, then proceed clockwise. Each player may retire each pensioner to a prize; the summary does not require retiring any pensioner. Pay the prize's printed cost, move the member to that prize and gain its printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends to determine display selection order, then pay it to the bank. Unused pensioners return to supply and do not remain for another turn.
answers.evidence: London Season → Retirements: starting order, may-retire rule, payment/member/VP movement and unused pensioners.

answers.answer: No. When an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital's starred flag; it is no longer an empire. The rule applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest.
answers.evidence: Components → India terminology: explicit last-dominated-region rule and cause independence.
Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘Firm-track VP per share’ schedule.
